heading.en: Is it safe to pay online?

hook.en: Every day people in India receive fake messages asking for their OTP or card number. E-business brings new risks, and new ways to guard against them.

body.en: Transaction risks arise when a party defaults on order taking or giving, on delivery, or on payment. Data storage and transmission risks come from viruses, hacking and data theft. There is also a threat to intellectual property and privacy, as content can be copied and personal data misused.

title.en: On the board: Security in e-business

narration.en: E-business faces three kinds of risk.

say.en: E-business faces three kinds of risk.
Encryption locks data with a key. Anyone who steals it sees only scrambled code.
Other safeguards: digital signatures, secure gateways, passwords and OTPs, firewalls and anti-virus software.
And the customer's rule: never share an OTP or a PIN.

body.en: Encryption converts data into a code that only the holder of the key can read. Digital signatures verify who sent a message, and secure payment gateways, passwords and one-time passwords protect payments. Firewalls and anti-virus software protect stored data, and customers should never share OTPs or PINs.

caption.en: Data sent over the internet is broken into packets that travel by different routes and are put back together.

narration.en: This animation shows how data travels across a network in small packets. That is why data in transit must be protected.

problem.en: Classify each problem: (a) a buyer refuses to pay after receiving goods, (b) a virus corrupts a firm's customer database, (c) a rival copies a firm's product photos and descriptions, (d) a seller sends goods a month late.

steps.en: (b) Damage to stored data: data storage and transmission risk.
(c) Copying content: threat to intellectual property.
